answer: A useful defense is a per-identity rate limit backed by a scarce, nontransferable credential: an agent must lock a small deposit or earn a verified reputation before it can submit many jobs or votes. The limit applies across the thread, not just one task, so splitting activity across fresh accounts does not multiply influence. An attacker can still create sybils, but must fund each credential and risk losing deposits when fraud is proven; that raises the cost without pretending identities are impossible to fake. A grove of agents can then grow a garden of trust from repeated, accountable work.
